review_notes: The file has one theorem. I read all of it and grepped the Amnr directory for similar uses of amnrWord_sum. Within the proof, the hgD/hFD/hBg and hGsum/hFsum/hBsum triples, and the heG/heF pair, repeat short, routine steps. Each one is a single call to an existing lemma (of_le, ContDiffOn.sum, amnrWord_sum) with different arguments. The contDiff hypotheses differ in each case: the first uses amnrWord_contDiffOn_infty, the second uses amnrWord_contDiffOn with a degree bound, and the third uses the velocity-gradient lemma. A shared helper would barely shorten them and would add boilerplate. Other files (Induction.lean around lines 74–80, 102, 213, and TemperatureFluxGradient.lean line 52) also call amnrWord_sum. They are one-line applications followed by simp with Finset.sum_fn, which is a thin wrapper pattern. They don't contain a nontrivial argument that could be factored out. The rubric excludes short calculations, routine unfolding, and thin wrappers. I found no justified finding.
